---
title: "Chapter 6: Validity"
---

Validity is perhaps the most fundamental concept in psychological measurement. While reliability asks *"does the measure produce consistent results?"*, validity asks the deeper question: *"does the measure actually measure what it is supposed to measure?"*. In this chapter we explore classical and contemporary accounts of validity, threats to valid inference, and how validity evidence is gathered and evaluated.
